name: tcpfit
description: tcpfit replaces copy-pasted sysctl recipes with real measurement: it detects your bandwidth-delay product and rate-limiter inflection point, then tunes TCP parameters per host. No fixed parameter guesses — every value is derived from what the machine actually sees on the wire. For anyone fighting flaky throughput on high-latency or rate-limited links, it turns black-box kernel tuning into an empirical process.
highlights: Detects BDP and rate-limiter inflection points per machine
Derives sysctl values from live measurement, not copy-paste defaults
Shell-based, no daemon or privileged agent required
336 stars and 41 forks in under a week
curatorNote: TCP tuning is normally folklore passed between sysadmins. Measuring the actual BDP and limiter inflection point per host is the rare empirical take that makes the advice reproducible.
